How Rare Coins Can Help Your Investment Portfolio

My comment in this article's comments section:

If there is one thing every coin investor should now, it’s the #1 downside to coin investing: Poor liquidity. Rare coins require a very specific buyer to achieve its full market value. That necessity – waiting for the right buyer – is the fundamental reason that coins and other hard-asset investments (houses, art, etc) are notorious for poor liquidity. Often, the more valuable a coin is, the longer it takes to sell it. If we’re talking about a large coin collection, it can take even longer to sell it all. It is not unusual for very rare coins to take months or perhaps years to sell.

Poor liquidity does help to discipline investors into giving the investments adequate time to mature. Lack of patience is the Achilles heel of many unsuccessful investors. Furthermore, coin investments are much like art investments – you are expected to “buy what you like”, and that is actually good investing advice is the coin market. Imagine the carnage if you tried to do that in the stock market! You see, a coin you like is probably appealing to other collectors too. Being likable gives a coin a popularity kick that both improves liquidity (surprise!), and its upside potential.

Truly, you are meant to enjoy coin investing. That more than makes up for the poor liquidity characteristic of coin investments. If you’re enjoying owning a coin, then there is no rush to sell it! A coin investor that thinks like a coin collector can easily turn the poor liquidity problem into an advantage. Poor liquidity in the rare coin market directly translates into safety and stability, which no other hard asset investment can match.

Coin collecting began as the “hobby of kings” because kings literally collected the coins issued by other kings, especially the kings they admired. Admiration of the coins themselves was completely natural, so coin collecting began at almost exactly the same time as coins were invented, thousands of years ago. To this day, wealthy people – modern day kings – still collect the coins they admire. After countless centuries, coin collecting and investing is unlikely to go out of style any time soon. That ancient fact is the source of safety and stability for today’s generation of coin collectors and investors.

So, the bottom line is, talk a little more about the poor liquidity of coin investments. Education and understanding about both the pros and cons of coin investing can easily equip people to turn any disadvantage into an advantage, in a well-diversified investment portfolio.
